properties.title: The Trust-Aware XAI (TAXAI) framework: a quantitative model for interpretable and reliable clinical AI systems
properties.membership_boundary: The documented main benchmark pipelines are not core healthcare world models. Component relevance is a separate judgment.

properties.source_path: Papers/091_2026_The Trust-Aware XAI (TAXAI) framework a quantitative model for interpretable and reliable clinical AI systems.pdf
properties.bibliographic_boundary: Read from supplied source material; no independent publisher lookup.
properties.supplements: Referenced but unavailable in this review.

properties.design: Author-reported computational demonstrations on public human-derived diagnostic benchmarks.
properties.contribution: Existing classifiers and explainers evaluated through a normalized Trust Index.
properties.execution_boundary: Author execution is documented; independent reproduction was not performed.
properties.human_evaluation: No human-subject experimentation; clinician-centered validation is future work.

properties.description: Mentioned exploratory tumor-kinetics evaluation using longitudinal brain MRI cases.
properties.boundary: Not equated with the main static Figshare classifier. Model identity, state, transition, horizon, data provenance, and predictive results remain unassessed.

properties.name: Trust-Aware Explainable Artificial Intelligence (TAXAI)
properties.pipeline: Independent diagnostic classifier → post-hoc explainer → fidelity, alignment, and compliance/reliability metrics → normalized Trust Index.
properties.top_level_constraints: Nonnegative coefficients summing to one; components normalized to [0,1].
properties.data_driven_weight_optimization: Explicitly an extension, not a reported optimization.

reported_sensitivity.TI: Variation less than 0.03 under moderate weight perturbations.
reported_sensitivity.boundary: Complete perturbation designs, paired outputs, and numerical uncertainty are not supplied.

properties.feedback: Conceptual development/refinement workflow, not demonstrated patient-state assimilation or clinical control.
properties.trust_boundary: Boundedness and score stability do not validate human trust, patient safety, cross-dataset comparability, legal compliance, or deployment readiness.

properties.scope_contract: Shared assertions concern only the six main-paper static benchmark pipelines and their TAXAI scoring composition. They exclude 091:study:supp.
properties.purpose: Research explanation evaluation, model comparison, auditing, and governance assessment.
properties.users: Developers and regulators are named; clinical experts appear in conceptual feedback and future studies.
properties.population_limits: Eligibility, evaluated-subset counts, patient/slide grouping, and dataset versions are incomplete.
properties.authority: No demonstrated execution of treatment recommendations, EHR writes, or device actions.

properties.tabular_split: 70% training, 30% held-out test; five-fold KFold restricted to training.
properties.tabular_TI: Fold-wise TI averaging is described; final held-out-test TI is not explicit.
properties.randomization: Tabular random_state = 88 given as an example; imaging described as three independent runs with fixed seeds.
properties.statistical_reporting: Mean ± SD, 95% confidence intervals, paired t-tests or Wilcoxon tests, effect sizes, and p < 0.05 are described; numerical uncertainty/test outputs are absent from Table 2.
properties.leakage_limits: Patient/slide boundaries, duplicate control, augmentation timing, fold-local ADASYN, and normalization fitting are not adequately established.

properties.name: LIDC–IDRI LightGBM with SHAP and ELI5
properties.version_boundary: Reported configuration, not a released checkpoint.
properties.unresolved: Image-to-feature derivation, labels, evaluated subset, and dataset release.

properties.name: NIH ChestXray-14 CNN with Grad-CAM
properties.unresolved: COVID-label provenance/additional cohort and detailed CNN configuration.

properties.name: Kaggle Lung Histopathology CNN with SHAP and LIME
properties.task_boundary: The listed classes do not establish a clinical stage target.
properties.architecture: Three convolutional blocks, 32 → 64 → 128 filters; pooling; BatchNormalization; dense 256; dropout 0.5; multiclass softmax.
properties.training: Adam; categorical cross-entropy; 22 epochs; batch size 32.
properties.time_boundary: Epochs are optimization iterations, not clinical time.
properties.modality_conflict: Named histopathology but also described as CT-derived/CT images.

properties.name: Wisconsin diagnostic LightGBM
properties.hyperparameters: 50 leaves; learning rate 0.1; feature fraction 0.8; maximum depth 12.
properties.preprocessing: ADASYN before fitting; fold-local placement unresolved.
properties.explainers: SHAP in Table 2; tabular Methods additionally name LIME and ELI5.

properties.name: Figshare Brain MRI CNN with SHAP
properties.boundary: Not identified with the supplementary longitudinal investigation.

properties.name: Pima XGBoost with SHAP and LIME
properties.task: Risk-classification benchmark; no declared future-state horizon.

properties.partition: Reported 70% training/30% test; five-fold CV within training.

properties.author_claim: Stable, comparable trust quantification and ethical/regulatory alignment; a layer is said to ensure fairness, reproducibility, and privacy.
properties.boundary: Computational aggregation does not establish human-trust calibration, privacy safeguards, legal compliance, or clinical readiness.

criteria_missing: Dataset releases and variable-level source/unit/timing lineage.
Resolution of modality ambiguity and fold-local transformation provenance.

assertions.rationale: Actual acquisition/event-time retention is not established. Runs and epochs are not clinical timestamps.
Feature-release timing relative to diagnostic queries is not audited; neither correct handling nor temporal leakage is established.
Observation-validity indicators are not established; supplementary preprocessing is unavailable. Saliency masks are not missingness masks.

assertions.applicability_reason: Independent diagnostic snapshots do not maintain carried-forward measurements in an asynchronous patient state.
The scoped static tasks contain no predecessor/successor time coordinate or prediction interval.

assertions.rationale: No conditional model of whether, when, or why clinical observations occur is specified. Attribution perturbation is different.

assertions.applicability_reason: No temporal resampling grid or timing-dependent target distinction is defined. Spatial resizing is not clock resampling.

assertions.rationale: Intensity/score normalization does not establish traceable clinical terminology and unit mappings; supplementary configurations are unavailable.
Splits and training-only CV do not establish patient/source-boundary audits or training-only preprocessing. Fold-local ADASYN remains unresolved.
Public-data use supplies no site-local retention or federated artifact-exchange protocol.
Reported CNNs map images to classifier features. Only the histopathology configuration has detailed layers; no evolving state follows from encoding.
No used pretrained checkpoint/adaptation is identified. Custom layers and training epochs do not establish from-scratch initialization.
The specified fitting procedure targets class labels through categorical cross-entropy, not target representations. Unknown earlier pretraining is excluded from this negative.

assertions.applicability_reason: Specified supervised CNN fitting and direct-feature LightGBM do not train predictive embeddings requiring this anti-collapse mechanism; unknown pretraining is excluded.

assertions.rationale: The specified fitting objective and output are label cross-entropy and softmax, not image reconstruction. Unreported pretraining is excluded.
Separate models analyze separate datasets. Combining explanation methods or F/I/C scores is not multimodal observation fusion.

assertions.applicability_reason: No joint multimodal fusion operation exists in the documented composition. Within-model missingness remains a separate reporting question.

assertions.rationale: Independent inputs map to static labels and explanation scores; activations, fitted parameters, and TI are not carried health-world states.

assertions.applicability_reason: No hidden evolving patient state is filtered. A classifier softmax is not a history-conditioned belief over such a state.
Static inference contains neither propagated state priors nor observation-conditioned state correction.
No individual forecast state is maintained. Proposed model-development recalibration is not patient-state assimilation.

assertions.rationale: No patient-specific parameter-fitting rule is reported. Domain-selected trust weights and generic recalibration do not establish one.

assertions.applicability_reason: No maintained world state exists to reuse across readouts. Reusing an audit formula across separately fitted models is framework reuse.

assertions.rationale: Feature-reduction benefit lacks a subset and matched results. Index-component ablation is not state-determinant sufficiency; supplementary ablations are unavailable.

assertions.applicability_reason: Scoped inputs are independent diagnostic snapshots, not subject histories used to infer a current evolving state or forecast.
No individualized trajectory forecast is evaluated. Local static explanations are not personalized dynamics.
No identity/anatomy is propagated through generated world states. Attribution stability is not transition-level identity preservation.
The component explains independent predictions, not maintained world-state coordinates. Attribution and decomposable audit scores do not supply that parent state.

assertions.rationale: Documented snapshot-classifier paths carry no subject history. Fitted weights, folds, and model-refresh feedback are not temporal memory.
Inputs are images/features, not separated settable healthcare commands. Occlusion, augmentation, thresholds, and index weights are analysis operations.

assertions.applicability_reason: No health-world action input exists to classify by role or effect channel.
No healthcare-action query requires dose, route, duration, or command-frame semantics.
No time-indexed intervention is queried. Epochs and repeated runs are not intervention schedules.
No joint treatment/device-setting intervention is represented. F/I/C aggregation is not treatment-bundle composition.
No candidate healthcare-action space exists. Simplex constraints bound index arithmetic, not clinical actions.
No clinical, robotic, or learned latent action requires an executable mapping.
No alternative healthcare regimes are queried; action overlap/support has no regime target.
No successors under settable healthcare actions are predicted. Comparing explainers, weights, or masks is not functional L3.
The experiment neither issues executable interventions nor actuates care/devices. This does not imply downstream score use is harmless.

assertions.rationale: The main operation classifies independent inputs and aggregates explanations; it does not advance health state over time or another successor coordinate.

assertions.applicability_reason: There is no health-world successor transition to classify as learned/hybrid. Learned classifier parameters are not learned dynamics.
Neither a world transition nor a settable healthcare-action pathway exists in the scoped mechanism.
No next-state process is defined. Softmax, dropout, randomized explainers, and run variability are not stochastic world transitions.

assertions.rationale: Permitted anatomical/literature scoring references are not demonstrated constraints on representation learning or predictive inference.
Narrative hybrid/neuro-symbolic superiority identifies no coupled mechanistic–learned configuration. Classifier/explainer/arithmetic composition alone is insufficient.

assertions.applicability_reason: No dynamics backend with state/action/time/successor semantics exists to exchange. Cross-model explanation scoring is different.

assertions.rationale: Separate datasets/tasks have no cross-scale state exchange. Three audit layers do not establish coupled biological scales.

assertions.applicability_reason: Documented training traverses no health-world transitions. Multiple epochs are not multi-step dynamics training.
No temporal transition process supports options/subgoals or multi-timescale coordination. Audit layers and CNN depth are different hierarchies.

assertions.rationale: Documented outputs are task values, attributions, and TI, not emitted observations from world state. Attribution overlays are not emission decoders.

assertions.value: Multiclass softmax on CNN features for Adenocarcinoma/Squamous/Benign.
assertions.rationale: A typed static readout is documented and evaluated; it supplies neither persistent world state nor clinical staging. No acceptance criterion is declared.
Scoped targets are static classes and explanation behavior, not later states or justified successor observations. This is nonperformance, not failed forecasting.

assertions.applicability_reason: No successor-state prediction chain exists to feed generated health states recursively.
No sequential forecasts or intermediate states exist to replace with ground truth. Supervised labels are not teacher-forced sequence evaluation.
No prediction/execution episode is followed by measured world-state correction. Development feedback is not re-assimilation.
Static classifications have no forecast extent. Epochs, folds, and threshold choices are not prediction horizons.
No forecast depths exist. Attribution/weight sensitivity is not free-running error versus clinical horizon.
There is no forecast-time axis or supported extent. TI sensitivity bounds are not forecast acceptance tolerances.
Static class probabilities and run variation are not conditional future trajectories preserving temporal dependence.
No temporal simulation request or supported forecast extent is exposed by the audit operation.
Proposed model selection uses explanation scores, not simulated health-world consequences; it is not the defined WM decision pathway.
No world-model action optimizer/policy exists. Adam fitting and policy-selected index coefficients are not such decision policies.
No plan, executed prefix, measured update, or planning/execution horizon exists. Model refresh is not replanning.
No learned transition is supplied to a planner. Changing audit weights does not demonstrate objective-independent dynamics.
No modeled-consequence action selection exists to modify through uncertainty penalties, constraints, or risk budgets.
No plans are optimized in a learned environment. Weight sensitivity is not planner-exploitation testing.
No candidate healthcare-action regimes exist. Classifiers, explainers, and occluded regions are not action candidates.
Three audit layers are not a goal/option/action policy hierarchy with duration and termination semantics.
Offline explanation evaluation does not involve actions changing an environment and resulting observations feeding later decisions.

assertions.rationale: Narrow distribution-representation judgment only; it establishes neither calibration nor validated uncertainty decomposition or posterior correctness.
F/I/C are audit components, not predictive aleatoric/epistemic estimators. Run variation does not establish separate uncertainty sources.

assertions.applicability_reason: Static outputs have no horizon-indexed trajectory or joint path whose reliability could be measured.

assertions.rationale: No predictive calibration acceptance target and measured attainment are supplied. ΔI and TI sensitivity bounds are not calibration tolerances.
No operational out-of-support statistic, threshold, and response is specified. Benchmark breadth and stability are not shift detection.

assertions.applicability_reason: Explanation evaluation targets no population intervention-effect contrast. Occlusion references are not clinical intervention estimands.
No clinical intervention-effect estimand is targeted. Attribution methods do not supply clinical causal identification.
No intervention effects are identified. Simplex, normalization, and statistical-test assumptions are not assumptions tied to a causal estimand.
No identified intervention estimate exists to stress for confounding/censoring/positivity violations. Weight/threshold sensitivity addresses another target.
No action-effect predictions require potential-outcome/interventional references. Diagnostic labels and occlusion masks are not counterfactual clinical ground truth.
No healthcare action enters a physical/pharmacological state-transition mechanism in the documented main implementation.
The score is not an intervention-effect or therapeutic-benefit estimate. Trust construct validity is a different assurance question.

assertions.rationale: No output/use blocking mechanism and fail behavior are specified. Score boundedness is not a safety guard; offline research does not make safeguards irrelevant.
No reject/defer trigger, withheld-output state, or fallback is specified. Low TI is not itself abstention.
Conceptual feedback supplies no operational trigger, available responder, timing, or fallback. Future human studies do not establish escalation.
No online hazard detector is connected to a protective response. Proposed dashboards and offline stability scores are insufficient.
Safe termination, degraded scoring, and fallback effects are not specified/tested; no physical emergency-stop requirement is invented.
Governance discussion defines no assets, adversaries, or attack paths involving data, reference signals, models, scores, and interfaces.
Generic input/threshold/weight perturbations lack defined attack or fault scenarios and measured safety-output consequences.
The privacy assertion supplies no operational de-identification, access, encryption, DP, federation, or minimization mechanism. Public-data use is insufficient.
No copying, membership, re-identification, or attribute-disclosure test is documented. Repeated-run agreement is not disclosure assessment.

assertions.applicability_reason: The benchmark operation has no external clinical/device read-write-actuation authority. Ordinary dataset access and future integrations require separate assessment.

assertions.rationale: Explanations and a trust-labeled score do not establish appropriate-reliance, override, or uncertainty-communication safeguards. Human-factors validation is future work.

criteria_missing: Permitted autonomy, approval responsibility, and enforceable downstream-use limits.

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/091_2026_The Trust-Aware XAI (TAXAI) framework a quantitative model for interpretable and reliable clinical AI systems.pdf
evidence_fragments.content:
To explore the potential extension of TAXAI toward longitudinal clinical prediction tasks, 
an illustrative tumor kinetics validation experiment using longitudinal brain MRI cases was conducted. The 
detailed experimental setup, regression evaluation metrics, and Trust Index computation for this exploratory 
study are reported in the Supplementary Information (Tables S9–S10).

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/091_2026_The Trust-Aware XAI (TAXAI) framework a quantitative model for interpretable and reliable clinical AI systems.pdf
evidence_fragments.content:
For datasets without explicit explanation ground truth, TAXAI constructs reference alignment signals using 
one of the following proxy strategies:
• Clinical priors: anatomically plausible regions (e.g., lung fields in chest imaging) extracted via standard seg-
mentation templates.
• Perturbation-based pseudo-ground truth: regions whose occlusion produces the largest prediction drop.
• Concept-level references:  ranked clinical features (e.g., perimeter_worst, concavity) derived from estab -
lished diagnostic literature in tabular datasets.

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/091_2026_The Trust-Aware XAI (TAXAI) framework a quantitative model for interpretable and reliable clinical AI systems.pdf
evidence_fragments.content:
Across datasets, alignment scores remained stable across thresholds, with variations below ΔI < 0.05 within 
small variation margins (ΔI < 0.05), indicating that Trust Index conclusions are not driven by a single threshold 
choice.

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/091_2026_The Trust-Aware XAI (TAXAI) framework a quantitative model for interpretable and reliable clinical AI systems.pdf
evidence_fragments.content:
Imaging demonstrations were conducted using a stratified 75/10/15 split corresponding to training, validation, 
and held-out test sets, respectively. The validation set was used for model tuning and early stopping, while final 
performance and Trust Index values were computed on the independent test set to ensure unbiased evaluation.

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/091_2026_The Trust-Aware XAI (TAXAI) framework a quantitative model for interpretable and reliable clinical AI systems.pdf
evidence_fragments.content:
For tabular benchmarks, data were first partitioned into 70% training and 30% held-out test subsets. Five-fold 
cross-validation (KFold, n_splits = 5) was applied exclusively within the training portion to assess robustness, 
and fold-wise Trust Index values were averaged. Final performance metrics were computed on the independent 
30% test set.

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/091_2026_The Trust-Aware XAI (TAXAI) framework a quantitative model for interpretable and reliable clinical AI systems.pdf
evidence_fragments.content:
All CT-derived images were resized to 224 × 224, intensity-normalized to [0,1], and augmented using rotation, 
translation, zoom, and horizontal flipping. A standard hold-out split (70% training, 30% validation) was applied.

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/091_2026_The Trust-Aware XAI (TAXAI) framework a quantitative model for interpretable and reliable clinical AI systems.pdf
evidence_fragments.content:
A convolutional neural network (CNN) classifier was implemented with three convolutional blocks:
• Conv2D filters: 32 → 64 → 128
• MaxPooling after each block
• BatchNormalization for training stability
• Dense layer (256 units) with Dropout (0.5)
• Softmax output layer for multiclass classification
Training was performed using Adam optimization with categorical cross-entropy loss over 22 epochs and batch 
size 32.

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/091_2026_The Trust-Aware XAI (TAXAI) framework a quantitative model for interpretable and reliable clinical AI systems.pdf
evidence_fragments.content:
Tabular benchmarks were evaluated using LightGBM classifiers trained on structured diagnostic features. Class 
imbalance was addressed using ADASYN oversampling prior to model fitting. Detailed dataset characteristics, 
including class distribution, acquisition context, and stratified data splitting protocols, are provided in the 
Supplementary Information (Table S6) to ensure transparency of the experimental setup.
Cross-validation and hyperparameters
Performance was estimated using fivefold cross-validation. Key hyperparameters included:
• Gradient boosting with 50 leaves
• Learning rate = 0.1
• Feature fraction = 0.8
• Maximum depth = 12

evidence_fragments.content:
Since TAXAI is a framework for quantifying 
trust in explanations rather than proposing a new predictive model, all evaluations are conducted by attaching 
established explainability methods (e.g., SHAP , LIME, Grad-CAM, ELI5) to standard ML/DL classifiers under 
controlled experimental settings.

evidence_fragments.source_ref: Papers/091_2026_The Trust-Aware XAI (TAXAI) framework a quantitative model for interpretable and reliable clinical AI systems.pdf
evidence_fragments.content:
All implementations were executed in Python (v3.10 +) using widely adopted libraries including TensorFlow/
Keras, Scikit-learn, LightGBM, SHAP , and LIME. Imaging benchmarks were evaluated on GPU-enabled 
environments, while tabular experiments were performed on CPU-based execution. Full hyperparameter 
configurations, confusion matrices, per-class metrics, and reproducibility resources are provided in the 
Supplementary Information. Confusion matrices are reported in Supplementary Fig. S1–S2, and per-class 
metrics in Supplementary Table S1–S2 (Table 6).
In the interest of transparency, all underlying data for this study are publicly available and were employed 
solely for methodological demonstration and framework-level evaluation; no proprietary clinical data or 
human-subject experimentation was conducted.

evidence_fragments.content:
Explainable AI systems designed for medical decision support may fall under the regulatory category of 
Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) as defined by the International Medical Device Regulators Forum (IMDRF). 
Under this framework, AI systems that analyze medical data and generate diagnostic or risk-assessment outputs 
are subject to regulatory oversight by authorities such as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) 48 and 
regulatory bodies operating under the European Union Medical Device Regulation (EU MDR) framework 49, 
along with similar national regulatory authorities.

legacy_cells.C: Mahua Pal; Himadri Nath Saha; Amlan Chakrabarti
legacy_cells.I: 091_2026_The Trust-Aware XAI (TAXAI) framework a quantitative model for interpretable and reliable clinical AI systems.pdf
legacy_cells.O: Lung cancer (benign/malignant, including adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma), pneumonia/COVID-19, breast cancer, brain tumors, and diabetes
legacy_cells.S: How can trust in explanations for clinical classification and risk prediction be quantitatively assessed and compared across models and datasets?
legacy_cells.DN: LIDC–IDRI, NIH ChestXray-14, Kaggle Lung Histopathology Dataset, Breast Cancer Wisconsin Diagnostic Dataset, Figshare Brain MRI Dataset, Pima Indians Diabetes Dataset
legacy_cells.DQ: NIH ChestXray-14 — 112,120 scans, Kaggle Lung Histopathology Dataset — 12,000 images, Breast Cancer Wisconsin Diagnostic Dataset — 569 samples, Figshare Brain MRI Dataset — 3,264 images
legacy_cells.FL: Standard ML/DL classifiers with explainers (SHAP, LIME, Grad-CAM, ELI5) feed fidelity, interpretability-alignment, and compliance scoring, then normalized aggregation into a Trust Index; no state-transition model or planner is described in the main Methods.
legacy_cells.FM: Proposes TAXAI, a normalized Trust Index combining explanation fidelity, interpretability alignment, and compliance/reliability to compare explanation behavior across models, datasets, and modalities.
legacy_cells.FN: Reported Trust Index values were approximately 0.85–0.94 across benchmark tasks. The paper reports threshold-related alignment variation below ΔI < 0.05 and Trust Index variation below 0.03 under moderate weight perturbations.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors state that the study is computational validation rather than prospective clinical deployment and that clinician-in-the-loop and multi-institutional validation remain future needs.
legacy_cells.FP: Automated trust dashboards, cross-institutional benchmarking, real-time multimodal interpretability, clinician-in-the-loop studies, and regulatory calibration.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors identify the lack of a standardized framework aggregating explanation fidelity, alignment with clinician reasoning, and governance/compliance into a comparable quantitative trust score.
legacy_cells.FR: The reported main-paper evidence does not demonstrate a persistent world state, a learned/hybrid state transition, action-conditioned forecasts, counterfactual rollouts, or planning/control. Results primarily concern static classifiers and explanation trust scores, not clinical benefit or prospective deployment. The paper mentions longitudinal MRI/tumor-kinetics work in supplementary material, but its methods and results are not present in the supplied main-PDF text, so that temporal claim cannot be verified here.
legacy_cells.FT: For an audit layer, keep fidelity, clinical-alignment, and compliance components separately interpretable, then aggregate them with explicit normalized weights; evaluate stability across thresholds and weighting choices independently of any forecasting or control claim.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF pp. 1–3 (title, abstract, introduction and claimed gap), pp. 4–8 (results and Tables 1–3), pp. 9–10 (discussion, clinical scope and methods overview), pp. 11–17 (methods, metric definitions, evaluation protocol and data tables), and pp. 18–20 (remaining text, references and declarations). | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I retained unchanged from prefilled metadata. The supplied 20-page main-paper text references an exploratory longitudinal brain-MRI/tumor-kinetics study in supplementary material, but does not include that study's methods/results; no WM state-transition evidence can be verified from the declared inputs. No table was unreadable in the supplied text. No external systems were accessed. Evidence QA: 23/28 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (82.1%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 26 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 2 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. limitations: Automated model review, not independent human verification, clinical audit, or experimental replication.
This synthesis received all main-paper text and earlier page-image review notes, not raw images. Visual coverage refers to the recorded earlier API page calls.
Supplementary Information was not supplied/retrieved. Its temporal study, statistics, ablations, runtimes, complexity, confusion matrices, and reproducibility resources remain unreviewed.
All 128 catalogue features have main-context dispositions, with model-specific exceptions. The uninspected supplementary study is not represented as a comprehensively reviewed model.
The supplied source hash was retained, not recomputed.
No executable schema validator, graph checker, file write, repository inspection, retrieval, or canonical admission was performed.
Author-reported illustrative benchmark execution is not independent reproduction.
Imaging partitions, histopathology/CT modality descriptions, COVID-label provenance, evaluated-subset counts, and patient/slide grouping remain unresolved.
Potential leakage is neither established nor excluded; augmentation, ADASYN, and normalization fitting boundaries are incomplete.
Dataset resource counts retain their original units and are not test counts or pooled patient totals.
Table 2 lacks numerical SDs, confidence intervals, p-values, and effect sizes despite reporting protocols elsewhere.
Histopathology TI 0.90–0.94 and F≈0.93/I≈0.91/C≈0.90 are retained unchanged; paired weights/components and rounding/run details are needed.
Anatomical templates, model-dependent occlusion references, and rank agreement are not actual clinician evaluation.
A compensatory bounded aggregate does not establish trust construct validity, clinical safety, legal conformity, or a clinical release threshold.
R2 is restricted to reported held-out actual-human diagnostic-classifier evidence, particularly Wisconsin. It does not validate TI against human trust or establish supplementary temporal capability.
No automatic R0 is assigned; worked arithmetic does not establish R1 clinical-simulation feasibility. Readiness facets are not inherited.
Article licensing is distinct from software, weights, and dataset terms.
Raw legacy cells, including historical reviewer statements, are preserved as supplied rather than endorsed as current evidence.
notes: Main result: a non-WM explanation-evaluation component with potential M9/M10 research relevance. Supplementary temporal capability remains unresolved.
